newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Medco says finds new oil reserves.
newsitem.headline: Medco says finds new oil reserves.

text.p: Indonesian oil and natural gas explorer PT Medco Energi said on Tuesday that it had found additional natural gas reserves of 200 billion cubic feet and new oil resources, both in South Sumatra.
The company said oil production would rise by 700 barrels per day but gave no other details on the find.
Company spokesman Dwi P. Bhakti said the find and rising international oil prices would lead to higher earnings for the company in 1996 and in 1997.
He told Reuters that Medco was confident of posting net 1996 income of 42 billion rupiah against an earlier target of 42 billion rupiah.
"For 1997, our net income target is 74.1 billion rupiah but we are confident we can reach 99.6 billion rupiah," he added.

He said the rises were due to the forecast increase in the production of oil and natural gas and also the rise of oil prices in international markets following the U.S. missile attack on Iraq last week.
"The total oil production capacity will increase by 700 barels per day from the existing 11,600 barels per day," Bhakti added.
Medco shares closed at 2,725 rupiah on Tuesday, up 375 rupiah.
